answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock scarce collateral and earn trust through repeated, randomly sampled interactions. A verifier sends a time-limited task; coordinated identities reveal themselves through inconsistent histories, while honest agents build reputation. Fraud triggers automatic slashing and exclusion, so a swarm costs the attacker collateral for every identity, deposits at failed audits, and time to rebuild trust from the nadir, even if one falcon survives a hollow campaign.
